evidence: The fallback branch used DEFAULT_TERMINAL_WIDTH raw while the wire branch went through getTerminalWidth's reserve, so `width` meant two different things depending on source; the fix routes both through one applyClaudeCodeReserve function.
guidance_note: When introducing a computed value with two paths to it (wire vs fallback), route both through the same transform before naming it a single field.

evidence: The demo computed width without the Claude-UI reserve while claiming to mirror production output; the fix applies applyClaudeCodeReserve in the demo too, matching real statusline bytes.
The comment pointed at test/daemon-autowrap.test.ts, a file that does not exist in the repo; the actual wrap coverage lives in test/strip-flex.test.ts, and the comment was corrected to match.

The diagnostic log line logging raw req.termCols alongside a width computed from the sanitized value was added in the same commit (16cf67e) that fixed F1; that extra logging line was new scope from the F1 fixup, and its own bug (raw vs sanitized mismatch) is what F4 reports.
guidance_note: When a fix adds new diagnostics alongside the required change, derive the logged values from the same sanitized binding used for logic, not a second read of the raw field.

evidence: The PR description (written before the F1 fixup deliberately decoupled MAX_DIAGNOSTIC_LINE_LEN from DEFAULT_TERMINAL_WIDTH) still claimed the two constants were linked; the agent updated the description rather than the code, one of the two paths the reviewer offered.
guidance_note: Update the PR description in the same push that changes the architectural claim it makes, not as an afterthought.

evidence: F1's fix unified the fallback path through getTerminalWidth(termCols), but that function itself falls back further to the daemon's ambient process.env.COLUMNS/stderr.columns when termCols is undefined -- reintroducing exactly the kind of source-dependent width F1 was trying to eliminate; verified via gh that 14f3688 (the flagged commit) only refactored the F4 log-line binding and did not touch this ambient-fallback behavior, so the defect traces to F1's redesign, not F4.
guidance_note: When centralizing a value through an existing helper for consistency, check what that helper does on every input path, including the one you don't intend to hit.

evidence: Flagged ON-NAMED-FIX-COMMIT 14f3688, but `gh api .../commits/14f3688` shows that commit only touched src/daemon/server.ts; the literal-glyph test assertion in test/strip-flex.test.ts dates to the original round-0 commit and is unrelated to any fix -- a late catch of a pre-existing style issue, not a consequence of an earlier fix.
guidance_note: Prefer escaped Unicode literals (\uE0B0) over raw glyphs in test assertions from the start, matching the codebase's existing constants convention.

narrative: The core F1 fix (centralize width-reserve application) was correct in intent but its unification through getTerminalWidth introduced an ambient-env fallback regression (F6), and the same fixup commit added an under-baked diagnostic log line (F4) and left a stale PR description (F5). Round 2 also caught an unrelated pre-existing test style issue (F7) that had nothing to do with any fix. Round 1 (F4, F5) was fully avoidable had the F1 fixup been scoped and self-reviewed more carefully; round 2/3 were not fully avoidable since F7 was independent.
guidance_observations: Scope-creep inside a fix commit (adding new logging, updating unrelated comments) creates new review surface that the original finding never asked for.
The agent's citations of [LAW:single-enforcer] and [LAW:no-silent-fallbacks] were accurate descriptions of the mechanism being built, not decorative.

evidence: A slash-bearing registered key would be listed by listStateKeys() but could never be addressed because set-state splits its wire tail on "/"; rejecting at registration keeps the registry surface equal to the writable surface.

Committing a batch with separate SessionState.set calls fired one MobX notification per key, so observers could see an intermediate state mid-batch; setBatch wraps all writes in one runInAction with one reportChanged, verified by a new test asserting exactly one observed snapshot.

makeAllowListValidator (present since the original round-0 commit 634769c, confirmed via gh) has the identical wire-splits-on-slash vulnerability that F1 fixed for registerStateValidator's keys, but the F1 fix (commit 7252eb0, confirmed to touch only registerStateValidator/SessionState) never swept the sibling factory in the same file.
guidance_note: When a fix rejects a structural class of input (slash-bearing values that a wire parser splits on) for one function, check every sibling function in the same file that consumes the same wire shape before closing the finding.

evidence: F3's fix (commit e912cc4, confirmed via gh) added only the slash-bearing-value check to makeAllowListValidator; the validator's own !raw check meant an empty string in the allowed list had the exact same unreachable-via-wire problem, left unaddressed by that same fix.
guidance_note: When adding a factory-time reachability check for one unreachable-value class (slash), check the factory's own runtime guards (the !raw empty check) for other values that share the same unreachability property.

narrative: F1 correctly closed the slash-bearing-key gap in registerStateValidator, but the identical gap in the sibling makeAllowListValidator (same file, same wire-splitting hazard) was not swept, costing round 2 (F3). F3's own fix then repeated the pattern at a smaller scale, closing the slash gap but leaving an analogous empty-string gap for round 3 (F4) to find. Two of the three post-round-0 rounds were avoidable if the agent had generalized the fix to the value side and to non-slash unreachability on the first pass.
guidance_observations: The agent fixed each finding narrowly and correctly but did not generalize the underlying principle ("a wire-splitting parser makes some values structurally unaddressable") across sibling validators in the same file, costing two extra rounds.
Law citations (types-are-the-program, verifiable-goals, one-type-per-behavior) were consistently apt descriptions of the actual mechanism.

evidence: extractWidgetRefs scanned raw {{ }} blocks without excluding string literals, so a widget name mentioned inside an unrelated string (e.g. printf "widget \"x\"") would be misread as a reference; the agent rewrote it to track code/string spans so only a real call keyword counts.

validateAction enforced the set/copy/open discriminator but never rejected unrecognized extra keys, unlike sibling widget/button validators, hiding typos like `too: "nord"`; the fix adds a per-arm allow-list of keys.

Widget cross-reference validation only checked seg.template, so a {{ widget "x" }} reference inside when/bg/fg would only fail at render time; the fix runs the same existence check across every template-bearing field.

validateButtonItem treated an empty-string glyph/label as present even though joinDisplay filters falsy strings out at render, producing a validated-but-empty clickable region; the fix treats empty string the same as undefined.
Exact duplicate of F4 (same text, same location, same fix); the fix treats empty string the same as undefined for glyph/label.

Verified via gh that requireSessionId (src/daemon/verbs/index.ts:93-97) already rejects an empty or slash-bearing session id at the click boundary before any set-state write happens, so the reviewer's claimed "malformed set-state write" cannot actually occur; the agent correctly declined to duplicate that check inside renderWidget (would violate single-enforcer) but did add the legitimate missing half -- a load-time requirement that a widget's set action have a session.id-bearing variable declared.
Exact duplicate of F1 (same text, same location, same fix).
Exact duplicate of F3 (same text, same location, same fix).
Exact duplicate of F2 (same text, same location, same fix).
Exact duplicate of F6 (same text, same location, same fix); requireSessionId already guards the click boundary as verified for F6.

validateAction's `set` case used requireString (type-only check) for the state key, so an empty string passed validation and would only fail later at click time; F4's fix (same commit 78d5ee8, same file) established the exact 'empty string must be rejected as absent' rule for button glyph/label but did not sweep it to this sibling code path in validateAction.
guidance_note: When a fix establishes 'empty string counts as absent, reject it' for one required-string field, check every other required-string field validated the same commit touches, not just the one the reviewer named.

evidence: Verified via gh that commit 046d659 (the flagged fix for F11) only touched validateAction's empty-key check; validateOnClick's failure to require a set action for optionsFrom buttons is original round-0 code (e967b21), a late catch unrelated to any earlier fix.

Verified via gh that 046d659 did not touch widgets.ts; the clickUrl comment's causality error (attributing slash-safety to the single decodeURIComponent rather than to keys/values being slash-free by construction) is original round-0 authoring, not caused by any fix.

validateWidgets built its record with a plain object literal, so a widget named "__proto__" could pollute the prototype chain; this is original round-0 code (confirmed the diff hunk's context is part of the initial 385-line addition), a late catch unrelated to any fix. Fixed with Object.create(null).
guidance_note: Any record keyed by a user-supplied config name needs Object.create(null) or a Map from the first commit, consistent with the pattern already used elsewhere in the same PR.

evidence: Option-picker active-marking read item.setKey as if it were the VariableStore variable name, but setKey is the SessionState key, which can differ from the variable name that reads it; original round-0 code, fixed by building a key-to-variable map from state-kind declarations.

Verified via gh that commit c1f5b38 (F15's fix) built stateKeyToVar only from config.variables (global scope); F16 found that segment-local state vars declared under segments.<seg>.vars use the same key-to-variable pattern and were left out of the map, so a segment-local picker never marks its current option.
guidance_note: When building a key-to-variable index for a feature that reads config.variables, also check segment-scoped declarations of the same kind before calling the index complete.

narrative: Round 0's ten comments were five duplicated findings, all real and cleanly fixed in one commit. That fixup (78d5ee8) itself left an analogous empty-string gap in validateAction (F11, avoidable round 1) by not generalizing the button-field fix to the action-field code in the same commit. Rounds 2 and 3 mostly surfaced pre-existing round-0 defects (F12-F15: an optionsFrom/action-kind gap, a stale comment, prototype pollution, and a key/variable mismatch) that Copilot simply took longer to notice -- these were not caused by any fix and were not avoidable via better fix discipline. Round 4's F16 was a clean incomplete_fix of F15: the state-key-to-variable map was built from global variables only and needed one more pass to cover segment-local ones.
guidance_observations: Two of six post-round-0 findings (F11, F16) were avoidable by generalizing an already-established fix pattern to a sibling code path in the same commit.

A notable share of findings across rounds 2-4 (F12-F15) were original-PR defects the reviewer simply hadn't reached yet, not consequences of any fix -- a more thorough author self-review before opening the PR (rather than during review) would have caught prototype pollution and the key/variable mismatch without spending rounds.
The two pushback findings (F6/F10, duplicates) were correctly and precisely defended by citing the actual enforcement point in the code (requireSessionId) rather than the law token alone.

evidence: release() used Array.shift(), an O(n) reindex per call, which under thousands of queued transcript ops would make a drain O(n^2); the fix replaces it with a head-index FIFO for O(1) dequeue.

Verified independently with `tsc --strict --noEmit` against a minimal repro (a gated() wrapper applied to overloaded functions with required parameters): it compiles cleanly. `(...args: never[])` is the maximally-permissive constraint under parameter contravariance, not a restrictive one, so the reviewer's claim that this fails typecheck for required-parameter functions is incorrect; the agent's pushback is technically correct and no code change was needed.

Verified via gh that F1's fix commit (d6a07d9) only reset the head-index queue on full drain, so under continuous saturation (queue never empties between releases) the consumed prefix accumulates without bound; the same fix's own reset condition was the gap. Replaced with a singly-linked FIFO where each dequeued node is immediately unreferenced, eliminating the accumulation regardless of drain pattern.
guidance_note: A head-index array queue that only reclaims its consumed prefix on full drain still leaks under sustained load; a linked-list or periodic-compaction queue is required if the workload can stay continuously saturated.

narrative: F1's O(n)-shift fix (head-index array) was directionally right but its full-drain-only reset left a genuine unbounded-growth path under sustained saturation, which F3 caught and fixed with a linked-list queue -- exactly the failure class this ticket exists to prevent. F2 was an incorrect reviewer claim about generic type variance that the agent correctly and precisely refuted; that finding coexisted in the same round as F3 so the round itself was not avoidable even though F3's content was.
guidance_observations: When designing a bounded queue specifically to survive sustained load, verify the reclaim/compaction strategy against a continuously-saturated workload, not just a bursty one, on the first pass.
The agent's pushback on F2 was independently verifiable and correct -- it cited the actual TypeScript variance rule rather than just asserting a law.

evidence: Coalescing keyed only by sessionId let a request that observed a newer transcript mtime attach to an older in-flight read and cache stale usage data; the fix keys by sessionId plus observed mtime so coalescing is result-equivalent to no coalescing.

F1's mtime-keyed coalescing fix shipped with no concurrent-miss test pinning the new keying contract; the agent added two tests, including one that would fail under the old sessionId-only key, directly verifying F1's fix.
guidance_note: A concurrency-keying fix (coalesce by X+Y, not just X) should ship with a test that fails under the old key, in the same commit as the fix.

evidence: The size property's comment claimed it was exposed for a daemon stats snapshot that does not read it; this is original round-0 authoring in single-flight.ts, unrelated to F1's usage.ts fix. Comment corrected to describe it as test/verification-only.

The class-level comment on CachedUsageProvider still said the in-flight compute was keyed by sessionId alone after F1's fix changed the key to sessionId+mtime, which the reviewer flagged as easy to misread as reintroducing the stale-read bug; comment updated to match.
guidance_note: When a fix changes a cache/coalescing key, grep the file for every comment describing the old key, not just the line the reviewer pointed at.

evidence: Verified via gh that F1's fix commit (0e6821c) touched only src/daemon/cache/usage.ts; today.ts's single-flight coalescing (present since round-0 commit 4636401, keyed only by calendar day) has the identical stale-attach vulnerability F1 fixed for usage.ts, and it was never swept to this sibling file introduced in the same PR.
guidance_note: When fixing a stale-coalescing-key bug in one file, grep the same PR's other new single-flight call sites for the identical unkeyed-by-freshness pattern before closing the finding.

evidence: The reviewer is right that a narrow staleness window remains (a probe in flight when a write lands), but the agent's rebuttal is sound: getLatestTranscriptMtime is a non-atomic multi-directory sweep, so even zero coalescing wouldn't guarantee the newer mtime is observed, the shared window is bounded to one probe duration and self-heals on the next probe, and the proposed revalidation-and-retry loop would reintroduce the exact redundant-scan storm this PR exists to eliminate. No further code change was warranted; the residual window is an accepted, documented trade-off scoped to a named sibling ticket.

narrative: F1's stale-read fix (key by sessionId+mtime) was correct but was applied to only one of the two single-flight call sites the PR introduced; the identical gap in today.ts surfaced in round 2 as F5, an avoidable round. F1's fix also left a comment drift (F4) and a missing regression test (F2) in the same file, both cleanly closed the next round alongside an unrelated pre-existing comment issue (F3) that made that round unavoidable regardless. Round 3's F6 was the reviewer re-flagging an irreducible property of a non-atomic freshness probe; the agent's pushback, backed by a specific architectural argument and a named follow-up ticket, was correct and no further round was warranted.
guidance_observations: A single-flight/coalescing fix pattern (key by full computation identity, not just an identifier) should be applied to every call site of the same primitive added in the same PR, not just the one the reviewer flagged.

The agent distinguished cleanly between 'a real gap this PR should close' (F1, F5) and 'an inherent property to document and scope out' (F6), rather than either over-fixing or dismissing the later finding.

evidence: registerDslConfig still pre-resolved globals.palette into a frozen per-segment resolver at registration time, so a session theme change would never recolor segments relying on the global default -- defeating the PR's entire stated purpose. The agent deleted the offending pre-resolution path (effectiveSegmentPalette) entirely and strengthened the regression test to catch a config-default freeze.
guidance_note: When a helper function's only purpose was the behavior a PR is explicitly reverting, delete the helper rather than leaving it as a trap for the next caller.

evidence: The barrel file's header comment still named transposed-resolver.ts as the implementation location after this PR renamed it to palette-resolvers.ts; comment updated to match the rename.
guidance_note: A file rename should be grepped for in every comment referencing the old filename in the same commit.

narrative: Both findings were real defects in the original PR: a critical one (the global-palette freeze that defeated the PR's live-recolor goal) and a minor rename-drift comment. Both were fixed cleanly in the single post-round-0 commit, and round 1 confirmed no new issues, so no round was avoidable or wasted.
guidance_observations: F1 was the most consequential finding in this batch relative to PR size -- it would have silently defeated the feature's stated purpose for the common case (a bundled default theme) had it shipped; worth flagging as a pattern (pre-resolving a value at config-load time that a later feature needs to stay live) to watch for whenever a PR's goal is 'make X live/dynamic'.
